gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-gfs-didot: Marker-straight strokes up top, with daylight inside every curve. GFS Didot sits below with a faint swing from thick to thin, and its generous curves keep a long page of serif text moving gently.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-gowun-batang: Red Hat Display draws every arm and leg at a constant width, which gives headings a firm, contemporary punch. Yet Gowun Batang, a classic serif, trims its terminals back to leave big gaps, and that is where it does its best work.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-habibi: Habibi has a clear channel running into each round letter. Under it, Red Hat Display looks cut from wire, so the heading stays stark while the serif text keeps its traditional, editorial warmth.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-hahmlet: Red Hat Display runs one flat line weight through every glyph, bold and contemporary from the first letter. Hahmlet, a serif with a slight charcoal-like pressure and widely parted forms, carries a longer read with a friendly, dignified ease.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-im-fell-englis: Red Hat Display keeps one flat, unswelling line around every curve. IM Fell English SC, a text serif with moderate contrast and open throats, gives that bold heading a bookish partner with some old-print character.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-inika: Contemporary and bold, the heading looks like cut ribbon of constant width. Inika, a classic serif with a visible gap in each s, then takes over with a more traditional voice beneath it.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-inria-serif: Refined and dignified, the body text comes from Inria Serif, a classic serif with wide-mouthed round letters. But Red Hat Display above it draws every stroke at one thickness, so the headline looks like marker work.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-joan: Wire-flat joints, bold and modern, with no thinning where strokes meet. Red Hat Display handles the loud part; Joan, with its gently tapering serif strokes, handles the quiet one.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-junge: Junge brings authority with gaps in its curves that stay generous and strokes that taper slightly. Junge, a text serif with respectable thin strokes, moves a longer page along steadily beneath the tubular, wire-like Red Hat Display.
gen-fs-red-hat-display-gf-kameron: Kameron curves lighten mildly toward the ends, and its curves refuse to close. Kameron, a classic serif, looks bookish under Red Hat Display, whose ruler-drawn line sets a bold, contemporary tone above.
